gates.detail: all derived columns reconcile to within 0.01 USD across 20 rows

flat markup %: 10.00 10.00 10.00 10.00 10.00  (sd 0.0000)
        implied annualised %: 10.0 20.0 10.0 40.0 20.0  (sd 10.9545)
        *** The flat markup is CONSTANT at 10.00%% while the implied annualised rate
        varies from 10.0%% to 40.0%% with tenor. A constant-rate loan in disguise would
        hold the ANNUALISED rate fixed and vary the flat markup. This schedule does the
        opposite, which cuts AGAINST the disguised-interest reading, not for it.
        Recorded as measured; this gate scores no verdict either way.

legal owner across all 5 periods: ['Bank']
        variable maintenance [500.0, 600.0, 550.0, 700.0, 650.0], total 3000 USD — billed INTO the lessee's payment: True
        *** Title stays with the financier while the lessee pays every maintenance
        charge. The ownership BURDEN has been moved without the ownership RISK moving
        with it. That is arithmetic on the rows, not an opinion — and it is the
        structural point the practitioner critique makes about lease wrappers.

property value across 10 months: min 400000 max 400000 sd 0.0000
        *** The recorded asset value NEVER MOVES. A co-ownership schedule with a
        constant asset value cannot exhibit co-ownership risk, because no event
        occurs for the co-owner to share in. This is the single most important
        finding in the audit and it is a property of the DATA.

maximum per-period cash-flow difference from the matched debt twin:
            murabahah 0.003333   ijarah 0.000000   musharakah 0.000000
        (tolerance 0.01 USD)
        *** ALL THREE ARE CASH-FLOW IDENTICAL TO DEBT AS RECORDED. The musharakah
        rental is exactly 0.6250% per month of the financier's outstanding stake in
        every period — which is the definition of a declining-balance interest
        schedule. This does NOT show the contracts are debt. It shows THE SUPPLIED
        DATA CANNOT TELL THE DIFFERENCE, because it contains no event at which a
        difference becomes visible.
